newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar ends firmer in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar ends firmer in quiet trading.

text.p: * Canada's dollar ended firmer on Monday at C$1.3690
(US$0.7304) from Friday's close of C$1.3697 (US$0.7300) in
quiet trading sidelined by interest in a weaker German mark.
* The mark fell to new lows against major currencies on
worries a broad-based European monetary union will produce a weak euro, creating uncertainty in Germany's currency.
The U.S. dollar stopped short of 1.80 marks on speculation that concerted central bank intervention could emerge to halt the rally.

Farrill said Canada's dollar would likely find its direction this week as economic statistics began to roll out, with Canadian wage settlements for May on Tuesday and consumer prices for Canada and the United States on Wednesday.
"All things are on hold until we start getting the numbers and they'll start coming out fast and furious tomorrow."
The Canadian dollar rose against the mark to 1.3127 marks from Friday's close of 1.3024 marks, but was relatively flat at 83.18 Japanese yen on Monday from 83.16.
